item.text:
**It is reasonable to raise the all-male panel as a concern, but it is not, by itself, evidence that the decision was discriminatory.** It raises a question about the bank’s approach to balanced recruitment; whether it breached any rule depends on the country and the bank’s policies.

Your qualifications make your question understandable. Still, the announcement alone cannot establish that you were the stronger candidate overall. A head-of-function role may place substantial weight on leadership, regulatory relationships, and management experience as well as technical expertise. Equally, “broad experience” is too vague to explain why he was preferred.

I would focus on **how the decision was made**, with panel composition as one part of that inquiry:

- Follow up on your unanswered request, asking for the selection criteria, their weighting, and an explanation of how your application was assessed against them.
- Ask what recruitment policies govern panel composition and how the bank safeguards against bias.
- Keep the job advertisement, correspondence, announcement, and your interview notes. In particular, record any comments about gender, family responsibilities, or leadership “fit.”

You could write:

> I am following up on my request of [date] for a written explanation of the appointment decision. Please clarify the selection criteria and their weighting, and how my qualifications and experience were assessed against them. I would also appreciate clarification of the bank’s policy on selection-panel composition and safeguards against bias, given that all four panel members were men. Please confirm when I can expect a response.

Two weeks without a reply warrants a follow-up, but does not itself show discrimination. If you are considering a formal complaint, check local deadlines promptly rather than waiting indefinitely for the bank.

**Which country was the position in?** That matters for both panel-composition requirements and any right to a written explanation.
